## TL;DR

I ran a QA pass over the Model providers panel and the API key save path, using fixtures and fake keys only. The pass found one data-loss bug, a few error messages with no next step, a missing Saved / Not set status, a hidden error on failed Clear, and a 375 px header overlap. I fixed all of them, added jsdom and headless WebKit tests at 375, 768 and 1280 px, and wrote the QA record in `docs/qa/2026-11-api-key-screens-qa.md`. Live provider calls were not made, so a human still needs to check a real key.

## Work and rationale

The panel (`ModelProvidersPanel.vue`) and the Model routing key form (`ModelRoutingPanel.vue`) both post to `POST /api/model-providers/:id/key`. I read the save path, the route handler, `setDotEnvSecret` and the provider error code before changing anything.

The most serious finding was data loss. The API reads an empty key as "clear", and `ModelProvidersPanel` sent whatever was in the field. So Replace key, then Save with nothing pasted, or Enter in an empty field, deleted the saved key. A route test already pins "an empty save clears the key", so I kept that API rule and fixed the UI instead. An empty Save is now refused with a plain sentence, and only the explicit Clear action sends an empty value. I applied the same guard to the Model routing key form, since it posts to the same endpoint.

Second, a failed Clear was invisible. Its error was rendered inside the key form, which is hidden once a key is saved. The error now shows on the saved row.

Third, the spec asks for Saved / Not set, and the panel had no status label. I added a pill beside each live key row. It does not appear on the Muse row, which reads a CLI login, or on link-out rows.

Fourth, the error text. The task asks for plain-English errors with a next step. I rewrote these paths:

- A rejected key (401) from OpenRouter, opencode Go or DeepInfra now reads "X rejected the API key. Check the key was copied in full, then use Replace key to paste it again." Previously it showed the upstream text with no next step.
- A network failure now reads "X could not be reached. Check your internet connection, then press Retry."
- A multi-line paste now explains that the key spans more than one line and asks for a single-line paste. Previously it showed "Secret value must not contain newlines".
- A failed `.env` write no longer returns the raw error, which included the file path. It says to check the repo folder is writable.

Fifth, layout. At 375 px the new status pill overlapped the "Open dashboard" link. I made the row header and title wrap and kept the link on one line. I checked this in the 375 px screenshot.

For the QA test I used headless WebKit, following the pattern already used by the #1223 Agents QA test. The real component is mounted in jsdom with a stubbed `fetch`, its markup is rendered in WebKit with the built global CSS and the compiled scoped CSS, and the test checks each state at three widths. The states are missing key, rejected key, unreachable provider, a save the server refuses, and an empty Save. Each state checks for off-viewport elements, the expected copy, a masked field, and no fake key in the rendered page. The test is `src/ui-app/tests/api-key-screens-qa-browser.test.ts`. It uses only fake values and never touches `.env`.

## Approaches tried

I considered changing the API so an empty key is rejected, and making Clear a separate endpoint. I rejected both. The route test documents empty-as-clear as intended API behaviour, and a UI guard fixes the accident without changing that contract. The guard also covers both forms in one place, since the server is the common point.

For the WebKit test I first copied the full harness, including the stub sidebar. The sidebar overflowed at 768 px and failed the audit. That was my fixture shell, not the product, so I removed the stub. The placeholder check also failed at first because placeholders are attributes rather than text. I fixed the assertion.

The WebKit page is static HTML, so it cannot test interaction. The clicks, the refused save and the empty-Save guard are therefore driven in jsdom before the markup is captured, and the WebKit test checks the resulting state.

## Challenges and blockers

The main challenge was that the existing tests pinned the old wording in several places: the 401 upstream text, the "Could not reach" text, and the newline error. I updated those expectations deliberately, so each change in wording is visible in the diff.

`vitest` must be run with `--config src/ui-app/vite.config.ts`. Running it from the repo root fails with a Vue SFC import error, so I used that config for every focused run.

No human step is blocked. The acceptance criteria still need a human for one thing: whether real OpenRouter, opencode Go or DeepInfra keys behave as the fixtures assume. I did not make live calls and did not use any real key. The QA doc says so.

## Key learnings

- A value that means "clear" on the server must never be the default value of a form field. Make the clear action explicit in the UI, and refuse an empty Save.
- Errors hidden inside a conditionally rendered form are invisible after the form closes. Errors for an action belong on the surface where that action was taken.
- Pin wording with tests when you rewrite it, because the old wording was pinned in mocked component tests as well as route tests.

## Verification

- Focused runs with `bunx vitest run --config src/ui-app/vite.config.ts` on the four affected suites (model-providers-panel, model-providers-routes, model-provider-spend, model-routing-panel): 106 tests passed. The new WebKit suite (api-key-screens-qa-browser): 15 tests passed. I reviewed the 375 px screenshots after the header fix.
- `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` ran once after `bun run fmt` and exited 0 with "All checks passed". Its test step was skipped locally because the suite runs on the remote validator, so the full suite has not been run here.
